newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 31.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Sources said most of Macau's influential triad chiefs blamed a gang leader nicknamed "Broken Teeth" Koi for the recent killings in the Portuguese-administered enclave, and were offering HK$2 million for his capture.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Xinhua News Agency said it would not be an overlord to the Hong Kong government, but it still hopes to keep some authority and intends to spread its influence through Chinese companies and coordinating election affairs.
-- WEN WEI PO -- China's exports in the first half of the year increased 26 per cent year-on-year. By June, foreign reserves had reached US$120 billion.
-- China's Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji said Beijing would try to help state-owned enterprises get out of their financial difficulties in three years' time.

-- SING TAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin ordered a campaign to strengthen the army's discipline. Sources said that as discipline loosened, many soldiers used public money on banquets and gifts and got involved in business.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Volatility continued to hit regional currencies yesterday, forcing the Taiwan dollar to a nine-year low and prompting the People's Bank of China to intervene to stabilise the yuan.
-- China's National People's Congress Chairman Qiao Shi has come under new pressure to retire and yield his position to Prime Minister Li Peng.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A Thai government deadline on finalising the financing of Hopewell's US$4 billion road and rail project was expected to pass today without agreement.
